title: Encode String with Shortest Length
summary: Given a string s , encode it using the rule k[encoded_string] , where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is repeated exactly k times, and k is a positive integer.
statement: Given a string s , encode it using the rule k[encoded_string] , where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is repeated exactly k times, and k is a positive integer. If encoding does not result in a shorter string, do not encode it. If multiple valid encodings exist, return any one of them.
constraints: An encoding contains lowercase literals and k[encoded_string], with positive integer k and a nonempty body. Nesting and concatenation are allowed.
Return any shortest encoding that expands to exactly s. If no encoding is shorter, return the literal input unchanged.
Several optimal strings may be accepted; this is not run-length encoding or merely finding the shortest repeated prefix.
target_time_complexity: O(n^4) upper bound with Python string construction
hints: An optimal expression is either literal text, two adjacent expressions, or a repeated expression.
Solve every substring from shorter lengths to longer lengths, trying all splits and exact repeat periods.
Initialize the substring answer to its literal text; improve it with left+right encodings and k[encoded_period].
Only replace an answer when shorter. The judge checks decoded text and optimal length, not which tied answer you choose.
editorial: The outermost grammar operation gives a complete case split: literal, concatenation, or repetition. Its children encode shorter substrings already solved by interval DP. Trying all splits and all exact periods therefore finds a minimum-length expression. Python substring construction gives an O(n^4) upper bound and stored encoded strings an O(n^3) space bound. The independent small-input oracle enumerates all non-lengthening parse-tree encodings, including ties. Bounded grammar decoding accepts equally short alternatives and rejects malformed or excessive expansion without eval.

tests.explanation: The literal aaa has length 3, shorter than 3[a] of length 4. Do not encode it.
10[a], a9[a], and 9[a]a all expand to ten a characters and have the optimal length 5. Any of these answers passes.
